  • Step 2: a card shows the focus ring: the card you focused last or, if no card has been focused yet, the first card in "Unassigned" ({Work-order-3}).

Chris Ward answered on 15 Oct 2026 (answer 28): Tab reaches every control, Enter opens, Escape closes, focus returns to the control that opened a menu or dialog, reassigning by keyboard goes through the ⋯ menu, and there is no keyboard drag. PRD version 54 rewrites Story 11 into these requirements, and this case now checks them.

Chris Ward's answer 28 (15 Oct 2026) and PRD version 54 said Tab reaches every row, card and header in on-screen order. PRD versions 55, 60 and 61 (15 and 16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward rulings on Slavcho Mitrov's questions and the QA triage of SV-11395, SV-11397, SV-11422 and SV-11421) changed this: each view is one Tab stop that lands on a work order, and the arrow keys move between cards, rows, headers and columns.   • S11-R3: “Inside a view the arrow keys move focus: Up and Down move between rows and group headers in Tech View, and between cards and the column header within a Board View column; Left and Right move between Board View columns. Tab from a focused row, card or header reaches its own controls (more actions, pin, collapse) in order, then leaves the view. Tab never stops on every row.”
  • S11-R9: “Assigning, reassigning and unassigning by keyboard go through the more-actions menu: Assign lead technician or Reassign lead technician (S3-R14) opens the lead technician dialog, and Unassign is a menu item. There is no keyboard drag in this release, so reordering work orders and technicians is by mouse or touch only.”
  • S4-R5: “After a successful lead change on Board View or Tech View, whether by drag, the dialog or Unassign, show the design’s toast (white, with the check icon) with an Undo button. It reads “{work order number} assigned to {technician name}”; “{work order number} lead technician set to {technician name}” when the new lead was already the technician on at least one of the work order’s lines; or “{work order number} moved to Unassigned” after removing the lead. Examples: “S1-357 assigned to Esther Howard”, “S1-702 lead technician set to Ralph Edwards”, “S1-352 moved to Unassigned”. This replaces the standard success toast for these messages only.”
  • Tech plan Phase 11 dialog: “The dialog is the keyboard path for moving work between technicians; it runs the same permission and status checks as the pointer path (S11-N1)”

SV-11416 asked the product owner what happens when a lead technician is deleted; the spec covered only a deactivated lead. PRD version 59 (16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward ruling on Slavcho Mitrov's question on SV-11416) added S3-R20e: such work orders sit under "Deleted technician" with the inactive marker and no grip, take no drops, can be dragged out, and List shows the lead blank (version 68 changed this to "Unassigned"). In versions 66 to 68 (19 Oct 2026) the message after a lead change became "{work order number} assigned to {technician name}", with Undo (step 10). This case follows version 59 and later (was: no "Unknown Technician" column, the header naming the technician as List does).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R20e: “Work orders whose lead technician was deleted in Settings → Staff (the name no longer exists) sit in one column on Board View and one group in Tech View labeled “Deleted technician”, with the inactive marker and no drag grip. Work orders can be dragged out of it; nothing can be dropped onto it. List shows “Unassigned” in the Lead Technician column for these work orders, as today.”
  • S4-N5: “Nothing can be dropped onto the column/group of an inactive technician (S2-N2, S3-N2) or of a technician who is not enrolled at this location (S3-R20c).”
  • S3-N4: “Show an inactive indicator on deactivated technician columns.”
  • S2-N3: “Indicate deactivated technicians as inactive in group headers.”
  • S4-R5: “After a successful lead change on Board View or Tech View, whether by drag, the dialog or Unassign, show the design’s toast (white, with the check icon) with an Undo button. It reads “{work order number} assigned to {technician name}”; “{work order number} lead technician set to {technician name}” when the new lead was already the technician on at least one of the work order’s lines; or “{work order number} moved to Unassigned” after removing the lead. Examples: “S1-357 assigned to Esther Howard”, “S1-702 lead technician set to Ralph Edwards”, “S1-352 moved to Unassigned”. This replaces the standard success toast for these messages only.”
